page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 belongs to the GPU Machines family, designed specifically for graphics and machine learning inference tasks. The instance provides 8 virtual CPUs based on 4 physical cores of an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.2 GHz, backed by 32 GB of system memory at a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration is delivered by a dedicated NVIDIA L4 GPU built on the Ada Lovelace architecture, featuring 24 GB of VRAM. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence, and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight an asymmetric profile focused on GPU throughput over host CPU computation. Host processor benchmarks, including Geekbench and single-core stress-ng tests, fall into the lower tiers, reflecting the moderate 2.2 GHz clock rate. System memory bandwidth and multi-core integer tests sit in the middle tier, with uncached read speeds around 50.64 GB/s and write speeds of 37.76 GB/s. In contrast, machine learning inference benchmarks achieve top-tier performance for small and medium language models, delivering 2,225.82 prompt tokens per second and 52.31 generation tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

The hardware configuration provides high cost efficiency for entry to mid-range acceleration pipelines where full datacenter accelerators like the A100 or H100 would represent excess capacity. However, architectural tradeoffs exist: the 24 GB VRAM ceiling precludes running large 70B parameter models without model partitioning or extreme quantization, and compute-heavy host tasks are constrained by the modest single-thread CPU performance.

The g2-standard-8 instance is best suited for real-time AI inference on models up to 7B parameters, computer vision processing, GPU-accelerated video transcoding, and graphics rendering workloads where a balanced CPU-to-memory host environment provides adequate support for GPU operations.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine tailored for graphics workloads and AI inference. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at 2.2 GHz, it features 8 vCPUs (4 physical cores), 32 GB of RAM, and a single NVIDIA L4 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM based on the Ada Lovelace architecture. The instance lacks bundled local storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on networked storage. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate modest single-core CPU performance alongside middle-tier memory bandwidth, contrasted by top-tier inference speeds for language models up to 7B parameters. The 24 GB VRAM envelope presents an efficient resource balance for small-to-midsize neural networks and media rendering, though it limits deployment of large 70B parameter models. Workloads suited for this server include real-time inference, image and video processing, and GPU-driven rendering pipelines.
